title: Evaluating agents as evolving systems
dek: A practical evaluation loop for agents that change with prompts, tools, and model upgrades.

stories.title: Google describes a hill-climbing workflow for agent evaluation
stories.dek: The unit of improvement is the complete agent system, not an isolated model score.
stories.evidence: Vendor engineering walkthrough; not independent results
stories.takeaway: Track full traces and per-case outcomes on a frozen regression set. Do not promote a model or prompt change based only on a mean score.

sections.title: What changed
paragraphs: Google published a technical walkthrough of Agents CLI's evaluation commands. Its workflow separates running test cases, grading traces, comparing runs, analyzing repeated failures, and optimizing prompts.
The sample evaluation shows how an apparently harmless system-prompt edit can reduce tool use and cause hallucinated answers even though code still runs correctly.

sections.title: Evaluation loop
paragraphs: The workflow uses eval generate to produce traces, eval grade to score them, eval compare to inspect differences, eval analyze to identify repeated failures, and eval optimize for selected prompt-optimization tasks.
Select each stage below to explore the corresponding engineering control.

sections.title: Numerical example
paragraphs: In Google's small illustrative test of four cases, the average response quality score fell from 4.00 to 2.75 on a five-point scale after a prompt regression. The example shows why teams should inspect per-case failures rather than treating a single average as a reliable release gate.
Four test cases are insufficient to estimate production reliability. The numeric example demonstrates a workflow, not a general performance benchmark.

sections.title: Application to financial AI
paragraphs: Create a fixed evaluation dataset with financial document retrieval, numerical reconciliation, source attribution, entitlement checks, and structured query execution.
Record full tool traces and compare candidates on task success, unsupported claims, unauthorized tool attempts, cost, retries, and p95 latency. Review per-case regressions before promotion.
